fullPassage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often efficient in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.

These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to ②<u>empathizes</u> strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often efficient in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and ③<u>force</u> us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and ④<u>employ</u> other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② empathizes → empathize: to부정사는 to + 동사원형
det.analysis:
✅ ① widely: 'widely praised'의 부사 — 적절
❌ ② empathizes → empathize: 'we tend to empathize'에서 to부정사이므로 동사원형 empathize ←정답
✅ ③ force: 'can further encourage ... and force us'의 병렬 동사원형 — 적절
✅ ④ employ: 'give up ... and employ other tools'의 병렬 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: tend to + 동사원형 empathize (empathizes 불가)

다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오.

"우리는 우리 내집단에 강하게 공감하는 경향이 있다"

[조건] (1) empathize, in-group, our, strongly, tend, to, we, with를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것
(영어로)

det.korean: we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group
det.analysis:
정답: we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group

(1) 주어와 동사 'we tend(우리는 ~하는 경향이 있다)'로 시작해요.
(2) 'tend to + 동사원형'이므로 to empathize(공감하다)를 이어요.
(3) '강하게'는 동사를 꾸미는 부사 strongly를 empathize 뒤에 놓고, '우리 내집단에'는 with our in-group으로 붙여요.
→ we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group (8단어)
det.tip: tend to + 동사원형, empathize with ~ (~에 공감하다)
